#6731. Safe Word: The Best Jewelry Launches of November 2026

Safe Word is a series highlighting the latest trends in the jewelry market, keeping you up to date on all things that sparkle and shine.

November’s jewelry launches are looking both backward and forward, with designers revisiting their roots, reworking archival ideas, and stepping into entirely new territory. First up, Quentin Jones is taking her surrealist art off the wall and onto the body with “Nocturne,” her first jewelry collection; Pomellato reaches back to 1997 to revive “Moneta Orientale” as a colorful modern talisman; David Yurman celebrates the magic of a New York holiday with Michael B. Jordan, Yerin Ha, and Inde Navarrette; Vhernier revisits its iconic “Trottola” design with new proportions and contrasting materials; Di Volpe reinterprets the classic tennis bracelet with customizable gemstones in “DiSegno”; Brent Neale transforms the classic bow into sculptural fine jewelry with “Wrap It Up”; and Kendra Scott launches the new “Kendra Scott Collection,” reimagining her signature Spike motif as a personal talisman. From archival revivals and meaningful motifs to innovative designs and new creative directions, November’s launches prove that sometimes the best way forward starts with looking back. For the rest of the month, we’ve got you covered on all the jewelry-related happenings worth knowing about.

Quentin Jones is taking her art off the wall and onto the body with “Nocturne,” the first jewelry collection from House of Quentin Jones. Following the multidisciplinary artist’s debut of surrealist ceramics and tapestries last year, the new collection transforms recurring gestures and symbols from her work into sculptural collars, cuffs, armbands, pendants, chains, and earrings. Eyes, hands, stars, moons, tears, and knots take shape in silver and gold vermeil alongside freshwater pearls, onyx, opals, jade, glass, and silk tassels, giving the pieces a dreamlike, talismanic quality. Beginning as drawings and hand collages in Jones’s Brooklyn studio, each design carries her surrealist visual language into wearable form, further blurring the line between art, design, and fashion.

Piotrek Panszczyk Makes His Debut at Ippolita

Ippolita is entering a new chapter under creative director Piotrek Panszczyk, who makes his debut at the house with “Ancient Bohemia,” a collection inspired by its archives and the organic forms of nature. Taking a sculptural approach to jewelry, Panszczyk reimagines familiar signatures with an emphasis on texture, craftsmanship, and unconventional layering. The house’s iconic Wavy Disk becomes the Wavy Coin, featuring Hippolyta, Queen of the Amazons and the brand’s namesake, as a symbol of feminine strength. Elsewhere, hand-sculpted Stardust pavé is set entirely with diamonds, pearls make their first appearance, and lightweight, hand-hammered silver Roma links offer multiple ways to wear, from necklaces to belts. Lapis lazuli, mother-of-pearl, and quartz introduce color through Ippolita’s signature layered doublets and triplets, mixed rather than matched for an eclectic finish. The result is a fresh interpretation of the house’s heritage that feels both ancient and distinctly modern.

Jade Trau and Luis Morais Combine Gemstones and Diamonds

Jade Trau and Luis Morais are joining forces for a limited-edition collection that brings together their different approaches to fine jewelry. Comprised of 16 one-of-a-kind pieces, including 12 bracelets and four necklaces, the collaboration pairs Morais’s colorful gemstone beads with Trau’s signature 18-karat gold and diamond elements. The designs feature a vibrant mix of stones, from chrysoprase and amazonite to lapis lazuli, turquoise, carnelian, and tiger’s-eye, accented by recognizable Jade Trau details like the Frankie rondelle, Sophisticate station, and Georgie diamond lock. Designed with everyday wear in mind, the bracelets lend themselves to layering, while the necklaces incorporate Trau’s diamond-set closures. The result is a playful meeting of color and craftsmanship that brings a fresh perspective to both designers’ signatures.

Lagos Looks to the Stars With Its Latest Collection

Lagos references the night sky in its latest fine jewelry collection, taking inspiration from the North Star and its centuries-old symbolism of guidance and possibility. Designed to celebrate milestones, new beginnings, and meaningful connections, the “North Star” collection features sculptural star motifs crafted in 18-karat gold and illuminated by natural diamonds. Cascading silhouettes and light-catching details bring a sense of movement to the celestial designs, balancing statement-making shapes with delicate craftsmanship. Both symbolic and sophisticated, the assortment offers a modern interpretation of a timeless emblem, making each piece a reminder of the people and moments that guide us.

Kendra Scott Launches an Eponymous Collection

Kendra Scott is offering a more personal look into her design world with the launch of the “Kendra Scott Collection,” a new line spanning fashion and fine jewelry. Its first edition, “The Spike,” revisits a silhouette the designer has worn throughout her career as a personal symbol of strength, confidence, and conviction. Inspired by nature and the radiance of the night sky, the collection translates the pointed motif into sculptural necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and charms, balancing bold proportions with intricate craftsmanship. Fashion jewelry incorporates tiger’s eye, malachite, and turquoise, while fine jewelry introduces lab-grown diamonds, pavé detailing, labradorite, and lapis. From statement-making links to delicate diamond charms, the collection offers a new interpretation of Scott’s longtime signature, inviting wearers to make the symbol their own.

Alison Lou’s ‘New Wave’ Collection Experiments With New Materials

Alison Lou is entering a new chapter with “New Wave,” a fine jewelry collection that introduces unexpected materials and a fresh approach to the designer’s signature playful aesthetic. Exploring the relationship between movement and form, the collection pairs lightweight titanium and ceramic with lab-grown diamonds, creating fluid, sculptural silhouettes that curve and catch the light. Available in Fig and Denim Blue colorways, the designs include wavy rings, diamond-accented signets, delicate thread necklaces, and statement drop earrings. With its unconventional materials and easy-to-wear designs, “New Wave” brings a new sense of movement to Alison Lou’s everyday jewelry.

Jenny Bird and Emese Gormley Partner on the Anyu Ring

Jenny Bird is expanding her JB FINE collection with a new collaboration featuring lifestyle creator and Lipstick on the Rim podcast host Emese Gormley. Named in honor of Gormley’s mother, the Anyu Ring offers a personal take on the classic signet, featuring three lab-grown baguette diamonds set in 14-karat yellow or white gold. The understated design combines the timeless appeal of a signet ring with a sentimental tribute to family, bringing a new perspective to Bird’s growing fine jewelry offering. Available exclusively on Jenny Bird’s website, the collaboration makes a case for jewelry that feels as meaningful as it looks.

Pomellato Revives Its 1997 Moneta Orientale Pendant as a Colorful Talisman

Pomellato is looking to its archives for its latest good-luck charm. For the newest chapter of “Memorie d’Archivio,” the maison revives Moneta Orientale, a 1997 pendant inspired by the ancient symbolism of a circle surrounding a square, representing the harmony between heaven and earth. Made in 33 stone-and-pavé combinations, the design pairs colorful hard stones including black jade, amazonite, sodalite, rhodochrosite, and labradorite with Pomellato’s signature irregular pavé of diamonds, sapphires, rubies, and more. Offered in two proportions, each pendant transforms the archival motif into a modern talisman for prosperity and protection.

Bibi van der Velden Makes Her High Jewelry Debut With ‘Eclipse’

Bibi van der Velden is entering a new era with “Eclipse,” the designer’s first high jewelry collection and most refined exploration of diamonds to date. Inspired by the fleeting moment when light gives way to darkness, the collection includes two six-piece suites: one in white diamonds and another defined by an ombré of diamonds into gray spinels deepening into black. Van der Velden’s signature alligator motif is abstracted into fluid, sculptural silhouettes, with scales engraved into the white gold on the reverse of each piece. “With Eclipse, I wanted to take those familiar elements and transform them into something more abstract and sculptural,” she says. “It’s a collection about transformation, which has always been at the heart of my work.”

Aflalo and Leandra Medine Cohen Turn Everyday Indulgences Into Fine Jewelry

Aflalo is finding the humor in our obsession with wellness with “The Vanities,” a new two-piece fine jewelry capsule designed exclusively by Leandra Medine Cohen. Playing with the contradiction between longevity and life’s little indulgences, the collection transforms two unlikely everyday accessories into precious objects. The Memento Mori is a 14-karat yellow gold cigar band set with more than four carats of diamonds, designed to slip over an Oura Ring, while The Libertine is a sterling silver pendant case adorned with diamonds and a wild-haired woman outlined in gold, designed to hold nicotine pouches or other small essentials. Equal parts extravagant and irreverent, the collection makes a playful case for enjoying life’s pleasures without sacrificing personal style.

Julia Berolzheimer’s Hart Jewelry Collection Draws on Childhood Memories

Hart is teaming up with Julia Berolzheimer for a new jewelry collection that celebrates the art of the stack. Inspired by Berolzheimer’s childhood memories of her grandmother’s California ranch and her collection of Art Deco minaudières, the collaboration brings together whimsical charms, colorful gemstones, and meaningful talismans designed to be mixed, layered, and restyled. Botanical motifs take shape in Tree of Life coins, daisies, bees, and fruit-inspired charms, while carnelian, turquoise, and pink opal add playful pops of color. One standout is the Perfume Vesta Case, a modern interpretation of a Victorian-era accessory that can hold a sample-sized fragrance and hang alongside other charms. With interchangeable chains, cords, and pendants, the collection makes a case for jewelry that feels just as personal as the memories behind it.

David Yurman Captures the Magic of a New York Holiday

David Yurman is celebrating the magic of the holidays in New York City with a new campaign featuring global brand ambassador Michael B. Jordan alongside actresses Yerin Ha and Inde Navarrette. Set against a snow-covered Washington Square Park, the campaign captures a series of quintessential New York moments, from Jordan and Ha facing off in a spirited card game to Navarrette hailing a cab in search of the perfect holiday gift. Throughout the campaign, the cast wears some of the house’s most recognizable designs, including 18-karat gold Cable bracelets and pieces from the “Starburst” and “Armory” collections. Directed by Bradford Young and photographed by Drew Vickers, the campaign brings together the spirit of the city, the joy of togetherness, and the timeless appeal of David Yurman’s jewelry.

Vhernier Reintroduces Its Iconic ‘Trottola’ Design With New Proportions

Vhernier is revisiting one of its most recognizable designs with a new interpretation of “Trottola,” the sculptural collection originally introduced in 2003. Inspired by the continuous motion of a spinning top, the latest designs play with proportions, contrasting materials, and asymmetrical shapes across rings, bracelets, necklaces, and earrings. Polished rose gold meets glossy black jet, with select pieces featuring diamond pavé for an added contrast of light and dark. The collection also focuses on versatility, from rings designed for stacking to convertible earclips that can be worn as studs or dangling earrings. With its fluid forms and unexpected material combinations, “Trottola” brings a fresh perspective to Vhernier’s signature sculptural approach to jewelry.

Di Volpe is rethinking the classic tennis bracelet with “DiSegno,” a new customizable fine jewelry system designed to change with its wearer. Using concealed, patent-pending connections, individual cultured diamonds and gemstones, called Elements, can be removed, rearranged, or added by hand, allowing wearers to transform bracelets into necklaces or earrings without compromising the seamless look of traditional tennis jewelry. The collection launches with 28 stone-and-cut combinations, including rubies, emeralds, sapphires, and diamonds, alongside a limited-edition collaboration with Lebanese artist Ali Cha’aban featuring five sculptural designs. With new cuts, colors, and artist collaborations planned for future releases, “DiSegno” makes the case for fine jewelry that’s never quite finished.

Brent Neale Riffs on the Bow in Fine Jewelry

Brent Neale is putting a bow on the holiday season with “Wrap It Up,” a new fine jewelry collection that transforms the familiar ribbon motif into sculptural works of art. Drawing inspiration from Old Hollywood glamour and the femininity of the 1960s, the designer plays with the contrast between rigid precious metals and the soft movement of fabric, crafting bows that twist, curl, and unfurl in 18-karat gold and platinum. Colored gemstones sit nestled within the ribbon-like forms, while pavé diamonds accentuate every curve and fold. Equal parts playful and precious, the collection brings a little gift-wrapped glamour to the jewelry box.

Grace Winfrey’s ‘Poppy Fortuna’ Collection Reimagines Good-Luck Charms

Grace Winfrey is bringing a little extra luck to the jewelry box with “Poppy Fortuna,” a new fine jewelry collection inspired by the natural beauty of the Italian landscape and symbols of good fortune. Scarlet poppies, sunflowers, bees, four-leaf clovers, horseshoes, and ladybugs come to life through vibrant gemstones and intricate pavé, creating miniature mosaics of color and texture. Highlights include a Lucky Bangle combining three good-luck charms, sculptural sunflower earrings with tiny ladybugs tucked into their petals, and layered charm necklaces designed to feel like modern keepsakes. Handcrafted in New York City, each piece transforms familiar symbols of prosperity, protection, and happiness into playful, colorful works of art.

Robinson Pelham Channels ’90s Glamour for Its Anniversary

Robinson Pelham is closing out its 30th anniversary celebrations with “Suite 96,” a new campaign and collection launch inspired by the glamour of late-’90s London. Set inside a private suite at St. James’s Hotel & Club in Mayfair, the campaign considers jewelry the ultimate room service, with diamonds arriving on trays, gold spilling out of wardrobes, and plenty of pieces to layer before a night out. At the center is “Studio 30,” a four-piece anniversary collection featuring diamond necklaces and statement earrings, including the sculptural Via and Hira necklaces, cascading diamond drops, and the bold Solstice Supreme. Alongside the anniversary designs, the house introduces new collections and additions to existing favorites, from chunky gold links and graphic heart rings to colorful enamel and gemstone combinations. Together, the launches celebrate three decades of Robinson Pelham’s bold, playful approach to fine jewelry.

Le Vian and Jared Revive Georgian-Era Romance

Le Vian is bringing a little old-world romance to Jared Jewelers with its new exclusive “Georgian Chocolate & Nude Diamonds” collection. Inspired by the candlelit jewels of the Georgian era, when jewelry was designed to capture and reflect the warmth of natural light, the collection rethinks historic buttercup settings in polished Honey Gold, with eight rounded prongs framing each natural diamond. The designs pair Le Vian’s signature Chocolate and Nude Diamonds with warm gold detailing across solitaire rings, anniversary bands, tennis bracelets, necklaces, and earrings. Select styles introduce colorful gemstones including Chocolate Quartz, Green Apple Peridot, and Grape Amethyst, giving the vintage-inspired silhouettes a contemporary update. With its sculptural settings and warm-toned stones, the collection brings the romance of antique jewelry into the present.

Wempe’s ‘Au:thentic’ Celebrates the Art of Goldsmithing

Wempe’s new gender-inclusive fine jewelry collection, “Au:thentic,” puts craftsmanship front and center, finding inspiration in the foundational skills taught to aspiring goldsmiths. The collection takes its shape from the jump ring, one of the first techniques Patrick Sieroslawski learned as an apprentice more than 22 years ago, translating its form to necklaces, bracelets, rings, earrings, and pendants. Handcrafted at Wempe’s atelier in Germany, the pieces come in 18-karat yellow, white, and rose gold, with select styles set with diamonds. “Au:thentic” also marks the beginning of a multiyear rollout, with three additional chapters set to expand on its design language through twists, wraps, and interlocking links.

Taylor Swift won’t miss a football Sunday. The pop superstar was back in her VIP suite yesterday to cheer on her husband, Travis Kelce, as he and his Kansas City Chiefs went up against the Arizona Cardinals.

#6728. Hold On, Did Grace Die on ‘The Body’?

Talk about divine intervention. Now that you’ve finished the first season of The Body, let’s talk about that ending. Specifically, what happens to Grace? Is she alive? Is she somehow more than that? How?!

At the beginning of the first season, Sofia Wylie’s character Grace is initiated into the dance team and given drugs at a house party as part of a “Satanic ritual.” The drug, ecstasy, causes Grace to pass out, seize, and seemingly die that night. The party took place at a building called Devil’s House... what did they expect? The girls try to cover up what they did by driving her home. But then, unexpectedly, Grace starts breathing again at the end of the episode. Is Grace just in a coma? That’s what they go with until things get weirder. It kind of becomes a whole thing.

Well, it was 2004. The Passion of the Christ was one of the highest-grossing films of the year. Everyone was doing the Numa Numa dance and just starting to get into Lost. If a teenage girl came back from the dead, it would be a huge deal. People would definitely try to cast her as a savior, which is what happens to Grace.

Lisbeth starts claiming she tried to resuscitate her, and that her survival is a miracle she performed. Meanwhile, Grace starts haunting some of the girls in their dreams. So, naturally, they start to ascribe meaning to her. Word spreads, and before long the whole town starts to worship.

In the finale, immediately after Anya confesses to what they did, Grace wakes up from her coma and says “I’m God.” She is risen? Literally, that’s what she says. (It’s also, for the theory-brained, the same thing Lisbeth says when she shows up at the infamous Halloween party because she dressed up as “slutty God,” complete with a toga and a giant crucifix. You know, just before she talks about being anointed.)

What did she mean by that? Does she even realize that she said it? Not only are Grace’s words bizarre, but doctors also conclude that she wasn’t even in a coma that whole time. All they’re able to conclude is that she was unconscious. Where was she?! What happened to her?!

According to Wylie, creator Quinn Shepherd has an explanation that the two of them are keeping to themselves for potential future seasons of The Body. “Quinn’s explanation is something I’d love to keep under wraps,” the actress told Tudum, “because I think the beauty of the show is that it stays within the mystery, whether it’s medical or spiritual.”

So, ultimately, it’s all a big mystery. We just have to have faith that The Body will get renewed for season 2 and continue this story.

#6727. Holiday Travel With Babies and Pets Just Got a Whole Lot Easier

Smart travel essentials for the whole family—four-legged members included.

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Seasonal travel is exciting, but getting everyone from point A to point B can be a production—especially when babies and pets are involved. Between navigating crowded airports, packing the car with what feels like half your house, and keeping your four-legged family members calm amid all the chaos, there’s a ton to think about. And while you can’t control flight delays, holiday traffic, or the timing of a much-needed diaper change, having the right travel gear can make a world of difference.

Enter Nuna and Tavo, two brands that bring thoughtful design, innovative safety features, and a beautiful aesthetic to (often hectic) family travel. Nuna’s premium baby gear helps take some of the stress out of everything from airport security to car-seat installations, while Tavo focuses the same level of attention on the safety and comfort of travel essentials designed specifically for pets. Think lightweight strollers that fold with one hand (because your other one is probably occupied), car seats that don’t require an online tutorial to install, and comfortable carriers that give your furry companions a safe spot of their own.

Whether you’re flying across the country to visit the grandparents, packing up for a holiday road trip, or exploring a new destination together, these six Nuna and Tavo essentials, available at Bloomingdale’s, can help make the journey a little more joyful for everyone involved.

Given crowded security lines, blowouts at the worst possible moment, and the sheer amount of stuff you have to tote, a lightweight stroller is a genuine lifesaver at the airport. At just 16.3 pounds, the Nuna VIAA cabn is designed to meet IATA cabin-size standards when folded with the armbar removed—though you’ll still want to double-check your airline’s requirements. One-handed steering makes navigating crowded terminals easier (especially when you’re juggling a much-needed iced coffee), while a roomy storage basket holds up to 22 pounds of diaper bags, coats, backup outfits, bottles, snacks, and approximately 47 things to keep your baby entertained. It even comes with a carrier bag for when it’s time to board.

This Nuna duo pairs the TRIV lx stroller, which folds with one hand and stands on its own, with the ultralight PIPA urbn infant car seat. And if you’ve ever broken a sweat or found yourself YouTubing car seat installation instructions for the 100th time, you’ll appreciate that this one clicks into place without a base, using its built-in pipaFIX rigid latch installation. Large rear wheels and all-wheel suspension pair with a spacious storage basket and handy tracking-device pocket to make the stroller ready for everyday outings.

The Nuna SWIV’s standout feature is button-activated 360-degree rotation on all four wheels, allowing it to move sideways and pivot through tight spaces without the struggle of squeezing through crowded airport lines and store aisles that clearly weren’t designed with strollers in mind. A one-handed recline with three positions, including a near-flat option, makes adjustments easy, and the stroller is travel-system-ready with any Nuna PIPA series infant car seat, allowing you to move baby from the car to the stroller.

The Tavo Crispin gives your pet a roomy, comfortable spot of their own, with mesh panels for ventilation and visibility so they can still keep eyes on their humans. It’s impact-tested and secures to your vehicle using lower anchors and a top tether, with a protective memory-foam guard for added peace of mind. And when the holiday travels are over, it collapses for easy storage without taking up precious space at home.

This Tavo travel system might be your new favorite on-the-road companion. The Maeve car seat attaches to the Roscoe Trek stroller frame, so you can go from the car to a festive outing without having to transfer your pup to a different carrier. All-terrain rear wheels and suspension make bumpy sidewalks easier to navigate, while one-touch brakes and a compact stroller fold come in handy when it’s time for a coffee stop or to load everything back into the car.

There’s a very particular type of heart-rate spike that comes with flying with a pet. You have to stand in the airline’s special-assistance line with your (probably nervous) dog or cat, only to finally reach the counter and hold your breath as the agent (and sometimes a supervisor) decides whether their carrier fulfills the rules. The Tavo Dupree II has a chic carry-on design that’s also crash-tested, complete with built-in vehicle connectors and a protective memory-foam guard. Mesh panels keep air circulating, while a trolley sleeve lets you slip it over your suitcase handle instead of carrying everything separately. You’ll still want to double-check your airline’s requirements before flying.

#6725. Bella Hadid and Nathan Lacy’s Low-Key Relationship Timeline Proves They’re Winning the Game of Love

From rodeo outings to sweet sightings, here’s how their love story unfolded.

Her name? Her name is Bella Hadid, and it seems she has a new man in her life. Oh, and he just so happens to be another cowboy. What can we say? Our girl Bella has a type, and she’s incredibly real for that!

The cowboy in question is Nathan Lacy, who she has been reportedly linked to since March 2026. They first sparked dating rumors when he was spotted trailing behind her during Milan Fashion Week, and now, they seemingly hard-launched at the boy aquarium a hockey game.

For the most part, Bella and Nathan have kept their romance out of the spotlight, but if you want to know how they met and when things started getting ~ romantic ~, you’ve come to the right place. Scroll through Bella Hadid and Nathan Lacy’s low-key relationship timeline ahead.

Before she started dating Nathan, Bella was linked to a different professional horseman: Adan Banuelos. The pair reportedly met at a horse show in Fort Worth, Texas, and dated for more than two years before calling it quits due to long distance and scheduling conflicts in early 2026.

“Bella is doing her best to stay positive and distract herself since their split,” a source told Entertainment Weekly at the time. “She's been staying busy with work and spending time with close friends. She is still processing the breakup since it was a very serious relationship."⁠

A source for Us Weekly announced that Adan and Bella were back together after a “brief but needed” split.

Per the insider, “They are working on their relationship right now. He has been a huge part of her life in Texas, so it’s been hard for her to let go.”

Amid Adan reconciliation rumors, Bella sparked romance rumors with yet another cowboy after Nathan was spotted walking with her during Milan Fashion Week. He was later identified as her friend Rachael Lacy’s brother, though neither addressed speculation about their relationship at that point.

Bella and Nathan were spotted grocery shopping together in Crested Butte, Colorado, over Labor Day weekend, per pics obtained by Deuxmoi.

Bella seemingly gave fans a clue about her relationship status in an Instagram photo dump following the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show.

Eagle-eyed followers noticed what appeared to be a photo of her kissing Nathan on her phone’s lock screen. What’s more: She deleted the pic from her dump shortly after.

After months of back-and-forth and a bunch of questions surrounding their relationship status, Bella and Nathan seemingly hard-launched their relationship during a Colorado Avalanche hockey game on November 7.

Bella also went Instagram official with Nathan, posting cute selfies from the game in her photo dump.

Then Bella’s cover story with Harper’s Bazaar dropped, and—though she didn’t reference Nathan by name—she did talk about her dream of “living in peace, in a small town, with a man that I love, with my child, having my animals.”

#6722. 6 Stylish Ways to Wear a Blanket Coat This Fall and Winter

Basically a blanket you can wear outside—and make it fashion.

Beating the cold has gotten that much easier with the rise of blanket coats. This winter, we’re staying bundled up, not only with stylish layering tricks like wraps, shawls, and capes, but by blending the two.

Blanket coats have become the cold-weather item fashion people are loving, and it was all over a lot of the fall/winter 2026 runways, too. So, it’s clear that the style is making the rounds, and there’s no need to wait for next winter to finally be tuned in. Blanket coats provide the coziness of at-home comfort, snuggled beneath a good quilt, to your everyday outfits.

And most serve a two-in-one purpose, also providing some neck protection, so you can opt out of scarves sometimes, or double up if you’re dealing with some really cold days. Below, I’ve gathered some stylish ways to lean into the popular blanket coat trend this fall and winter.

If you’re looking for something that feels a bit elevated, try a blanket coat similar to this style with draping that bunches and gathers flawlessly, giving an almost regal vibe.

If you’re not big on layering, let the coat do the layering for you. Leaning into a blanket jacket like this one that’s split open at the front makes it look like you’re wearing more pieces than you actually are.

The blanket coat serves as a literal wrap-around sweater that keeps you cozy and stylish. This black with brown trim one is perfect for your every day.

While some blanket coats wrap, others fall like trenches, but carry a bit thicker material like the one above. Pairing a simple neutral-colored piece with a monotone outfit is the easy way in.

The best part of a good blanket style coat is that it keeps you covered without having to deal with a zipper. If you want a more relaxed-fit coat then a style like this is great.

For those days when you wish you could carry around a big blanket with you, try instead pulling out your thickest coat that gives all the vibes.

#6717. Where Does Sunrise on the Reaping Rank Among the 6 Hunger Games Movies?

Warning: Spoilers for all six Hunger Games movies.

With the release of Sunrise on the Reaping, Suzanne Collins continues to expand on The Hunger Games movie franchise. The latest installment tells the story of Haymitch Abernathy’s Hunger Games—which doubles as the Second Quarter Quell, where twice the number of tributes are reaped—and details his journey from a humble member of District 12 to one of the most important forces in the Second Rebellion by the time Katniss Everdeen’s story is told. But how does Sunrise on the Reaping stack up against the other five films? Read on for ELLE’s ranking below.

Catching Fire ends with a major cliffhanger. When Katniss shoots the arrow that breaks the 75th Hunger Games arena, it kick-starts the true beginning of the revolution. It also provides one of the most heartbreaking plots in the series—when Peeta gets left behind during Katniss’s rescue from the arena, she’s forced to continue her rebel duties without having Peeta by her side.

The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes tells the story of Lucy Gray Baird, the first District 12 winner of the Hunger Games, whose Games have been erased from history. The film also provides much-needed insight into President Snow’s background, setting the stage for his years as a ruthless authoritarian. To restore his family’s reputation, Snow (Tom Blyth) mentors Lucy Gray (Rachel Zegler) in the 10th Hunger Games, but ends up forming an attachment to her that turns romantic. After Lucy wins the Hunger Games, she runs away with Snow so they can have a future without Capitol rule—but when she catches him in a lie that hints at his dangerous nature, she flees. The betrayal haunts Snow for the rest of his life and inspires him to make the Hunger Games even more vicious.

Before Katniss, there was Haymitch Abernathy’s Hunger Games. The second of the prequel movies, Sunrise on the Reaping shows Haymitch (Joseph Zada) before he became the jaded, embittered drunk that we meet in the first Hunger Games film. Haymitch isn’t entirely disillusioned by the government’s treatment of the district, but being forced to enter the games under such intense circumstances radicalizes him so much he’s inspired to take action. His hopes to spearhead the rebellion don’t pan out the way he had hoped, but that failure paves the way for a future where another rebel could be successful.

The dramatic conclusion to the entire franchise. In Mockingjay: Part 2, the conflict between President Snow (Donald Sutherland), the Capitol, and the outlying districts comes to a head, with the rebels working towards ending his authoritarian reign. Katniss, backed by her own personal army, successfully infiltrates the Capitol and finds it turned into a massive Hunger Games arena before she can successfully capture and kill Snow. The final film isn’t afraid to deliver surprising punches, with Prim dying while helping children in the Capitol and Katniss killing Alma Coin when Snow was meant to be her original target.

The movie that starts it all. Viewers are introduced to the world of Panem and its poorest district, District 12, on the day of the reaping ceremony, in which one girl and one boy are selected to participate (and likely die) in the Hunger Games. Katniss’s sister, Prim, worries about being selected to fight in the Games in her first year of eligibility—when Prim is selected, Katniss bravely volunteers in her sister’s place and rekindles the fire of the rebellion by nearly eating poisonous berries with Peeta while under the impression only one of them could win.

Devoted fans and critics agree—Catching Fire is easily the best film of the Hunger Games franchise. After Katniss survives the 74th Hunger Games and returns home alongside Peeta, the stakes are higher and the challenges are more complex than they were during her first trip to the arena. After being reaped for the Third Quarter Quell, Katniss finds herself fighting among skilled victors while unknowingly being at the center of a plot to overthrow the government. What follows is the true beginning of the rebellion and the battle against the Capitol and President Snow.

#6712. The Art of the Winter Layer

Use these cold-weather staples from The North Face for practical warmth with polished style.

Every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Like any specialized skill set, winter layering is one that must be continually practiced and perfected, lest your talents wane. It’s not as easy as throwing on a pair of cashmere leggings and a coordinating hoodie—that’s only the beginning. From there, it takes a careful curation of hero pieces (like puffer jackets and parkas), as well as a cast of supporting details (hats, gloves, and high-performance footwear), to layer effectively and aesthetically in the harshest conditions.

That said, even the most adept artist is nothing without an arsenal of trusted creative tools. And in these bitter temps, you’ll want to reach for the best, which essentially means any piece of gear with The North Face’s iconic rectangular logo attached to it. The storied brand has dominated the outdoor space for decades, having perfected the art of elevated style at elevated altitudes.

As we head into the chilliest season of the year, look to The North Face’s vast selection of dependable staples for all your layering needs. Designed both for performance and appearances, these pieces are in it for the long run.

Whether painting or dressing, it’s essential to start any creative endeavor with a blank canvas made of quality materials. A good base should be versatile and simple to pair with a host of helpful staples. Long-sleeve tees, cashmere turtlenecks, and crewneck sweatshirts, for example, are all good jumping-off points.

If you’re looking for a high-performance piece with enough style power to stand on its own, we recommend the Women’s Chabot 2.0 Mock-Neck. This cozy layering top offers the same reliable comfort of a traditional insulated thermal with a few modern updates. Though understated by design, its delightfully oversized fit and a funky waffle knit texture make the basic feel intentional and interesting.

For a closer-fitting base, the Women’s Golden Ridge Ribbed Long-Sleeve Tee layers easily under other pieces. Its slim fit and ribbed texture give this practical layer a polished look, while thumbholes at the cuffs add a functional detail. Bonus points for the tee’s anti-odor technology that helps keep the fabric feeling fresh.

Women’s Golden Ridge Ribbed Long-Sleeve Tee

After you’ve selected the first layer, the next stop should be your coat closet. This is where you’ll select the hero of your look. While each piece of the layering puzzle is uniquely important, the power jacket is a non-negotiable. The right iteration should supply a thick layer of warmth, while also doing its part to make the outfit, as a whole, feel cohesive.

Those who crave a more subdued winter aesthetic will love the classic appeal of the Women’s Arctic Bomber. The waterproof winter jacket boasts all the utility of a parka, with the sleek design details most commonly found in trend-focused outerwear. In four comforting colorways, this winter coat is an insulation powerhouse in a chic, wearable package.

Look to the Women’s Hydrenalite Down Jacket for a more classic puffer. This work-horse is a versatile down layer that can be slipped on at any time to keep you warm for any duration that you spend outdoors, whether you are on the mountain or running around town.

For the more artistically inclined, try the Women’s Yumiori Off Peak Full Zip Jacket. This fleece outer layer offers unfailing warmth and a distinctly sporty flavor. Its two-tone color palette, meanwhile, adds a fun, whimsical feel to the utilitarian, zip-up-style silhouette.

During the summer months, it’s all about the mani-pedi. But once that icy weather blows in, self-care starts to look a bit different. The North Face’s Etip Gloves are basically a hand treatment on the go. Crafted from soft, stretchy fleece made with 93% recycled polyester, these tech-friendly gloves will keep your hands comfortable on cold-weather outings. They’ll also keep you connected: Touchscreen compatibility lets you check your phone without taking them off, while silicone grip dots on the palms help you hold onto your device as well as smaller essentials like keys and credit cards.

For footwear, the Women’s THERMOBALL Traction Mule V will quickly become the standout of your seasonal lineup. These cloud-like slip-ons pair warm insulation with a quilted upper that gives them a casual, streetwear-cool vibe. The rubber outsole adds traction for quick trips outdoors.

The minimalist philosophy requires you to take off one item before leaving the house. But during the cold weather season, it’s in your best interest to do the opposite. As you walk out the door, make sure you grab a beanie since most of your body heat can escape from your head.

Beanies are simultaneously the most underappreciated outfit addition and the most indispensable. The North Face’s Wool Blend Beanie, for instance, pairs the warmth of its 65% merino wool knit with a refined, metropolitan style. Its classic cuffed design and textured knit add visual interest, while its deep fit offers roomier coverage. If you prefer the rectangular logo with the same cuffed look, you can never go wrong with the rib-knit and soft lining of the Salty Lined Beanie. On the slopes or on your morning commute, either will add a polished finishing touch.

The importance of a functional winter hat cannot be overstated—think of it as the final brushstroke in the art of winter layering.

#6711. Your First Car Comes with Questions

You’ve manifested several milestones—job, apartment, a squad of ride-or-dies. Now, you need a way to get from one to the other. This is where State Farm comes in as your trusted partner to help you make informed decisions. Here’s what you’ll need to know before you enter your car owner era.

As images of weekend getaways and road trips with your besties fill your mind, so, too, should these pre-purchase considerations.

At the dealership, put on your negotiation face. Buying a car is a little like dating—you do need to be observant, but you shouldn’t put all your cards (in this case: your budget) on the table. Finally, don’t be afraid to walk away. Follow these tips to make sure you're setting yourself up for success.

Before you turn up your favorite song and hit the open road, make sure your new baby is protected. It can be a lot to take in, so let’s demystify insurance. Here’s what you need to know.

Rate: This is the baseline estimated price that would cover the potential cost of future claims. It’s determined using shared group factors such as age group; if you’re in your twenties, it would take into account the statistical driving information for other 25-year-olds in a region.

Premium: This is the adjusted individual insurance price that you’ll pay over a six- or 12-month period. It’s created by starting with the rate, then adding more specific factors that affect your claim risk level. These include your driving record, claims history, mileage usage, and vehicle type.

Overwhelmed? Don’t sweat it—State Farm can get you an insurance quote before you buy.

Ah, the eternal question. Are you commitment-minded or more of a free agent?

To answer that when it comes to car ownership, consider how much you drive annually (to avoid leasing mileage overages if you exceed the stated mileage), how long you plan to keep your vehicle, and your financial situation.

Then, know that there are insurance differences between leasing and buying, too. Leasing companies adhere to stricter requirements than those that most states set, which could translate into higher monthly premiums.

If you buy to avoid the mileage caps and wear-and-tear of leasing, but still want the benefits of a fresh ride every few years, there is a moment during your payment plan when you can get a new car. Your initial loan payments largely go to interest (what lenders charge for giving you money), but there’s a break-even point when your payments begin going to principal (the actual amount you’ve borrowed). When that happens, and the outstanding balance is equal to the value of the car, you can trade it in for that amount, which is a budget-friendly way to upgrade.

Whatever you choose, a little strategy will keep you in the driver’s seat from dreaming about your new car to signing on the dotted line.

State Farm is there to protect you and your car.

#6708. A Complete Timeline of the Cyrus Family Drama, From Tish and Billy Ray’s Divorce to Miley’s Wedding

Here's where Miley stands with her parents and siblings.

Miley Cyrus’s family has had so much drama going on over the last four years, I can only assume producers over at E! are currently trying to sign them up for a reality show. And tbh, we’d tune in. But if you haven’t been Keeping Up With the Cyruses, gather round because it’s equal parts complicated and messy.

The short version: Everyone picked sides when Tish Cyrus and Billy Ray Cyrus got divorced, but after years of feuding, it seems the family may have buried the hatchet to all come together for Miley’s wedding...for now, anyway. Baffled? Same, so let’s dive in.

Tish filed for divorce from Billy Ray in April 2022, and they released the following joint statement to People:

I mean, sounds pretty chill! But Tish has since claimed she put up with “disrespect in every form” during the marriage, so...it seems like there was more going on behind the scenes than fans initially thought.

In fact, just a few months after Tish and Billy’s split announcement, a source told E! News that “the divorce between her parents has put a strain on [Miley’s] relationship with her dad and it’s been hard to connect with him in the last year. She hopes they can eventually work on their relationship.”

Tish married Prison Break star Dominic Purcell in August 2023, and the internet was quick to clock that neither Noah Cyrus nor Braison Cyrus were in the bridal party (whereas Miley Cyrus, Brandi Cyrus, and Trace Cyrus were).

Instead, Noah and Braison seemingly spent the day chilling at Walmart and posted a selfie that featured Noah in a Billy Ray Cyrus t-shirt.

A few months after, a source confirmed to Us Weekly that Noah has “always been close with Billy Ray,” adding that this has also “caused a rift between her and Miley.”

Oh, and another insider claimed, “The family dynamics haven’t been the same since the divorce, and now that Tish and Billy Ray are with other people, there’s even more division among them all.”

While Miley and her sister have historically been close, fans spotted the first signs of drama in October 2023, when Noah wrote, “The disrespect in this video...” in the comment section of a clip of Miley on The Joe Rogan Experience.

Right around the same time, Billy Ray married Firerose—but it’s unclear whether any of Billy’s children were in attendance.

After winning an award at the 2024 Grammys, Miley left Billy out of her acceptance speech, and a source later told Us Weekly that he’d been attempting to reach out with congratulations.

“He’s tried reaching out to Miley many times and congratulated her on her Grammys,” the insider said. “The kids have chosen sides, but friends are hoping the rift doesn’t last forever. Miley and Billy Ray are on the outs. Miley’s very close with her mom and is standing by her.”

Another source put it more simply, saying, “Miley hasn’t gotten over the disrespect she feels Billy Ray showed Tish and the family.”

Later on in the month, in a truly wild plot twist, an insider alleged to Us Weekly, “Noah was [seeing] Dominic when Tish started pursuing him,” adding Tish “was aware" of the situation and that “the turmoil between Noah and Tish goes far beyond [what people think]. Noah is very distraught over Tish stealing Dominic from her.”

Important note: Tish later claimed that she and Dominic met via DMs and did not mention anything about Noah...

Us Weekly also spoke to a source who said, “Noah and Tish haven’t spoken since the whole thing happened with Dominic,” and that “Tish is spiraling out of control and trying to figure out how to defuse this.” According to this person, Noah and Dominic were dating for “about eight to nine months” but were “having issues.”

However! The Daily Mail spoke to an anonymous insider who claimed, “Noah never dated Dominic and they were not together. She is delusional to think otherwise and is trying to create a narrative that will paint her as a victim.” This source emphasized that “Noah was not invited to Tish’s wedding and she would not have come even if she was. Tish wanted a peaceful wedding and did not want Noah to create any sort of scene.”

The insider went on to add, “Noah has always craved the attention because she did not get it growing up. Tish was always so Miley-sided because that is where the money was. Miley and Tish are like sisters and Noah has always been envious of this because she’s never had a connection with Tish like Miley has.”

When it comes to whether or not Miley knew about Noah and Dominic, sources differ. One person told People, “Miley had no idea about the drama with Dominic” and “confronted her mom about it,” while another told Us Weekly that Miley “absolutely knew” and was “fully aware.” Yikes!!!!

Yep! The musician shared a birthday message on Instagram for her mom in May amid the duo’s alleged feud alongside the caption, “Happy Birthday Mom.”

Aaaaaaand by July, the two were seen out and about together in Los Angeles.

During her My Next Guest Needs No Introduction episode, which aired in June, Miley explained (per E!), “Honestly, my mom is my hero. My father—I’m grateful for being able to watch him ahead of me. He’s almost given me this map. There is a map of what to do and what not to do. And he’s guided me on both.”

She continued, “My dad had a really rough childhood. And my childhood—I mean, we can go and talk about the hard times or the struggles—but I had food, I had love, I grew up in a beautiful big house and my dad didn’t have that.”

Miley’s rare comments were aired amid Billy Ray filing for divorce from Firerose after seven months of marriage due to irreconcilable differences and “inappropriate marital conduct.”

Following his dad’s performance at Trump’s inauguration Liberty Ball, Trace posted an open letter to Billy on Instagram, expressing concern for his health. Trace noted, “Me and the girls have been genuinely worried about you for years but you’ve pushed all of us away.”

He went on to add, “Noah desperately has wanted you to be a part of her life and you haven’t even been there for her. That’s your baby girl. She deserves better. Somehow just like me she still idolizes you though.”

Apparently, Billy Ray later threatened him with “legal action” for his public plea, because three days later, Trace followed up with since-deleted IG note, explaining that his open letter “was beyond loving” and that he “could have been extremely honest about a lot more.”

Billy ended up making a cryptic statement, saying, “Giving thanks for the California Rain . Praying for the brokenhearted and their pain. Praying for my family. For my children … sons and daughters…and their mother. Let this moment be the start of healing ❤️‍🩹 for us all. ‘The past does not equal the future.’ Amen.”

After Trace’s open letter to Billy Ray went viral, Braison (who helped Billy produce his latest album) took to his IG Stories to respond to his older bro, noting that their dad was “happy, healthy, and ready to make this record.”

A fan then slid into Trace’s DMs to question Braison’s post, and Trace replied with this cryptic message: “Birds of a feather flock together.” Well then!

Meanwhile, a “Cyrus family source” told People that family was attempting to work things out. “They got through the drama of 2024, and it’s a new year,” the source said. “Miley and Noah and Braison and Tish, they don’t want to be this Cyrus family feud. This is not enjoyable for them.”

Per a source for People, “Miley used to feel overwhelmed by the family drama. She worked hard to remove herself. She’s not about to get involved again. She’s in a great place now. She’s thriving and looking out for herself.”

For Braison’s 31st birthday, Miley and her fiancé Maxx Morando joined Billy on his farm in Tennessee, and her dad snapped a cute selfie to prove it.

During a profile with The New York Times that same month, Miley revealed that she and Billy have healed their bond. “As I’ve gotten older, I’m respecting my parents as individuals instead of as parents—because my mom really loved my dad for her whole life, and I think being married to someone in the music industry and not being a part of it is obviously really hard,” Miley said at the time. “And so I think I took on some of my mom’s hurt as my own because it hurt her more than it hurt me as an adult, and so I owned a lot of her pain.”

She added, “But now that my mom is so in love with my stepdad, who I completely adore, and now that my dad, I see him finding happiness, too—I can love them both as individuals instead of as a parental pairing.”

The following month, during an interview on Monica Lewinsky’s podcast, Miley opened up about “Secrets” off the deluxe edition of her album Something Beautiful.

“I wrote this song about my dad, because I wanted him to tell me even though there were secrets, even though I didn't really want to know,” she explained. “I wanted to be the one he felt safe enough to tell me the things that were damning and damaging to the family. I wanted him to think that as a middle child, I’m old enough that I could take some of that.”

She also talked about where her family stood in general, saying, “My family and I have had a really difficult…What did you call your decade? Dark decade. Yeah, we had one of those.”

She continued, “Half of us weren't speaking to each other at one point, and we cleaned all that up. That was a really important part of my year this year, was all of my family putting those lines of communication back together. A lot because of, you know, I had a lot of loyalty to my mom, the way that families do when parents get divorced.”

Miley sat down with her mom and sisters for an interview with The Cut, where it was revealed that the Cyrus ladies are all on good terms.

At one point, Miley said, “One thing I’ve always loved about our family is that we’re very honorable and respectful of each other’s differences; I think a lot of families get torn apart from their differences...but as we’ve gotten older, we’ve found our own opinions and ideas individually.”

To celebrate 20 years of Hannah Montana, Miley starred in a TV special, during which both of her parents made appearances.

Miley tied the knot with Maxx in Palm Springs, where—according to a source for People—“the most special part was seeing Miley’s family all come together to celebrate her.”

In attendance were Miley’s parents Tish and Billy, Billy’s girlfriend Elizabeth Hurley and her son Damian Hurley, Tish’s husband Dominic, Miley’s sister Noah and her fiancé Pinkus, and Miley’s sister Brandi and her fiancé Matt Southcombe.

It’s unclear, however, whether Miley’s brothers Trace and Braison (or her half-brother Christopher Cody) were there.

#6707. Bella Hadid’s Radical Vulnerability

Every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

How do you stay open in an industry that demands toughness? Bella Hadid embarks on a new chapter with a renewed sense of optimism and her boundaries firmly in place.

I first met Bella Hadid on a fashion shoot I was styling more than a decade ago. We went on to shoot several stories together, including her first major American magazine cover. On one of those shoots, she arrived upset because she had just found out she didn’t get cast in the Victoria’s Secret show. I will never forget telling Bella that one day, Victoria’s Secret would be begging her to walk for them. Cut to today, and Bella is not only one of the most in-demand models, but she opened their most recent show. When I saw her hit the runway in a beaded floral bra and matching wings, I let out a scream because I knew what that moment meant to her.

A few days after the Victoria’s Secret show in October, Bella and I sat down to reflect on her career so far, forgiveness and success, turning 30, and where she goes from here. I have always felt connected to Bella because she, like me, is a heart-on-her-sleeve kind of gal. She is deeply vulnerable and human, and it’s what makes her one of the most compelling figures in fashion today.

Samira Nasr: This is a full-circle moment. On one of our first shoots together, you were really upset because you didn’t get the Victoria’s Secret show. And I said to you, “One day, they will be begging you to be in their show.” And I could tell you didn’t believe me. Your whole body shut down. And three days ago, you opened Victoria’s Secret. Holy shit.

Bella Hadid: I still don’t believe you, to be honest. I feel like people are just AI-ing me onto the runway. I think that it’s so crazy how time passes and you still have some kind of impostor syndrome. No matter how hard you work, there’s always another girl who is more deserving, more beautiful, and has worked so hard to be able to get that spot. Ten years ago, I remember that moment too, where I never thought I would get the show, but I think that God always has a plan, and I truly believe at that time I wasn’t ready. I don’t think I’ve been ready until this year, to be honest. In past years, I was going to my horse-show finals in the morning, flying straight to the Victoria’s Secret show that day, doing rehearsal right before, and then pulling what we call a Bella, and Belinda comes out, and we just act. But this year, I felt really strong.

I have had to make a decision for myself to have boundaries with my own health. And I think it’s gotten me to this point now where I’m able to do the jobs that I do want to do with people that I love, that I can feel inspired by. And that’s truly what [working in] fashion is about: being around people you feel inspired by. Until you find that inspiration, it’s hard to go back into our industry. I think I needed a little bit of time just to be able to be like, “Let me just remember why I’m doing this again,” because I know I’m more than just a face.

SN: We don’t really support a culture of care. I have always believed that boundaries are bridges.

BH: They really are. We know so many people who have been working for 30, 40, 50 years in this industry with zero boundaries. I’ve watched people over the years just get more depressed because they don’t know themselves and they don’t know who they are. And that’s how I was for 10 years, when I didn’t know what my favorite color was, what I liked to eat. I stopped listening to music. To not be able to know yourself in an industry that tells you how to be every single day is really hard.

SN: Going back to Victoria’s Secret, did you feel empowered, or was that your alter ego? What is her name again?

BH: Belinda. You know what? Fortunately and unfortunately, I think it was Bella this year.

BH: I made up my alter ego, Belinda, a long time ago to deal with the intensity of everything happening in my life. So she could deal with that, and I can deal with this, and we can do this together, which I’m realizing I should probably go to therapy about again. Belinda is the one that people are like, “Wow, this, that.”

I have POTS [postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome], and I have a lot of PMDD [premenstrual dysphoric disorder], endometriosis, plus my Lyme and things that affect my body very deeply. Right before I walked out on the runway for my opening look, I went to go stretch and my whole clavicle completely … I don’t even know what it was. My lungs almost collapsed, and I couldn’t breathe, and then it was like, “Five, four …” So my body goes through these different motions of feeling really good and then all of a sudden crashing on me at the worst moments. I need to realize maybe my body can’t handle all that I have going on. Because I know how to walk. One thing I can do is I can strut. But it’s a lot of pressure; we all have our own insecurities. Sometimes my body just can’t connect with my brain. My brain wants to do it, and my body is like, “No, we can’t do that today.” And I’m like, “Okay, great. So let’s figure out another way.” But I think people don’t realize how much I struggle with the fatigue and the body pain, and so I just try my best.

SN: You’ve achieved so much in your 20s. You just turned 30. What are you looking forward to in your 30s?

BH: It’s funny, today I woke up with—I wouldn’t say the word is anxiety, but this feeling of “Oh my gosh, my life is starting.” I want to get rid of what doesn’t bring me joy and bring in what does. I’ve tried to put myself in positions for work for a very long time that have made me feel out of body or like I don’t belong. Years ago, I was just grateful to get a job, and I would say yes to everything. I lacked boundaries then, but I do believe that that gave me the strength to be able to have the confidence in my own boundaries now. I’ve achieved pretty much all the goals that I wanted to when it comes to fashion as a model. And now I do want to go into other ventures to eventually get to peace and happiness and love within this universe that God has put me in.

In the next couple of years, it’s just about getting back to community, getting back to using my voice again. I got beaten down pretty heavy for a long time, which pushed me into this very big struggle with my physical and emotional health, which makes my brain turn off and makes me not be able to write or read. When you’re not around enough people that are like-minded, you feel really ostracized. That’s almost where I got to. Of course, I always want to speak from my heart, which I hope will never disrespect anybody, but still be able to have the confidence to speak my truth and hope that people will walk beside me along the way when it comes to that.

SN: Is there something you’re most proud of achieving?

BH: Well, first and foremost, starting [my fragrance line] Orebella was something that I truly needed for my own creativity and to be able to build community. I am not a 50/50 person. I’m an all-in type of girl. Being able to move forward into my 30s, really focusing on building the things that I’ve started—Orebella was something that I pushed so hard for since 2018, and the fact that it’s really now coming to fruition makes me so proud.

When I was 17, going to my first go-see with a stylist I will not name, I was basically told I was too big to wear Saint Laurent and needed to lose a couple of pounds. And that’s when I was just a baby coming out of high school. Twelve years later, now I’m the face of Saint Laurent. I’m the face of Prada, which is incredible and insane. Times have changed so much, and the people that have come into the industry to make it a better place for us as models are so important. Not that that comment ever impacted me. I went through enough struggles with my body before that, so by the time she said that, I was like, “Okay, girl, I’m actually coming out of something that I dealt with very heavily when it came to my body. And now I look at food in a different way, and I love my body, and that’s okay if you think that I don’t look the way that you think I should look.”

I just would love for everyone to think about if every day they had to walk outside and be photographed, what that would feel like, because it’s an uncomfortable feeling for anybody. My face would change so much. I would be super puffy one day, and one day I would look yellow and emaciated, and people would think I was on drugs or doing this or that. And when anybody knows about, one, hormones, just as a woman in general, and two, about immune problems and how weight fluctuates—again, I just think that there needs to be more sensitivity in our industry.

SN: I’m curious if you’ve always been this person—so sensitive, empathetic—from a little girl.

BH: I’ve always felt like my sensitivity and my openness were a disservice to myself because I felt like no one else was like me in those ways, so I shut it down. Now I realize that there is a generosity of thoughtfulness that is so much deeper than just buying somebody an expensive gift. I think sitting on the side of the street with somebody, even if you don’t have any money, is more important than just walking by without caring.

SN: You’re able to access compassion when a lot of people can’t, and that is a superpower. I want to talk about style because you mentioned your archive. I remember you once mentioned you collect Gaultier. Do you still collect?

BH: I do collect. Behind me are bags to sell. But downstairs, I have my Gaultier dress that the atelier made. It was a Naomi Campbell dress that she had worn in one of their shows, and I was obsessed with it. I called their PR, and within a week and a half, because that dress was in a museum, I had it made and sent to Cannes, and that was that white-and-black dress that I wore on the carpet. And so, that’s here. My Coperni dress is here. I have a whole section for Virgil [Abloh].

SN: The last time I saw Virgil was with you, actually.

BH: I don’t think I’ve done a real, full Fashion Month since he passed away. And Vivienne [Westwood] and Karl [Lagerfeld] passed, and I felt like all of my idols were leaving, and it felt really scary. I have all the art Virgil gave me, his letter he wrote me, his bags, his shoes he made me. And then I have my Prada area, my Cavalli area, my Bob Mackies that I’ve been collecting over the years.

BH: Hopefully for a future wedding. There are just some dresses you can’t find again. And Bob did it best.

SN: He’s an American icon. I wanted to talk to you about Cannes. You’re such a queen of Cannes now, and I look forward to seeing you there. Is it fun?

BH: This past year was fun. I felt grounded. To do the red carpet and feel, in those moments, sober and happy and healthy and strong, and go to sleep not having anxiety about going out or how I’m going to look the next day, and just being with loved ones. It did really well for me this year.

Cannes has always held a very special place in my heart. It begins long before I arrive. Working closely with designers on custom gowns, exchanging references, and watching those first sketches come to life is such a beautiful part of the experience.

This year, being there to support Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo’s Ben’Imana, the first Rwandan film in the official selection, was especially meaningful. It explores memory and reconciliation after the genocide against the Tutsi through women whose lives carry its legacy. That’s what I love about cinema: It brings us closer and gives stories too rarely heard the attention they deserve. You can enter a theater knowing nothing of someone’s world and leave carrying a little of it with you.

SN: I look at you and how hard you’ve worked for so long, from our first job together. To me, it feels like you’ve achieved so much. But what does success look like for you? Do you feel you’ve achieved it?

BH: I talked to my business manager yesterday, so that made me feel a little bit more successful. But when you don’t think about the money part of it, I think success truly comes from peace within. At the end of the day, I really don’t need much. That’s why I do give back so much, because a lot of the money that I do make, I don’t feel deserving of. There are so many people in the world, whether it’s doctors or teachers, that I think deserve my pay rate a lot more than I do.

From an external space, success is about how known you are, how much you make, how many times you can be on TV, how many covers you’re on, how many fashion shows you do. And that is really important in our industry, especially when you’re building. But for me, I am different. Success, for me, can be living in peace, in a small town, with a man that I love, with my child, having my animals. I’ve always wanted to start a farm-to-table bakery, with flowers, and everything comes from the community. I want to do things that are fulfilling for me in my soul: having a greenhouse that I can garden in, having my glassblowing and ceramic studio, and having lots of children and being a mother. It wasn’t a dream that I’ve always had, but it’s something that now is so intense for me. My intuition is screaming so loudly at me about it.

I think knowing there is a reason behind everything is so important. My sister and I donated a million dollars to Palestine last year [the donation was split between HEAL Palestine, Palestine Children’s Relief Fund, World Central Kitchen, and United Nations Relief and Works Agency], which we could have never been able to do without the success that we’ve had.

God gave me the platform to be able to speak about the things that I hold dearly to me. And when it comes to Palestine or Sudan or Congo or Rwanda or places that mean so much to not only myself but the people around me—to give people a voice in any capacity, that’s success for me as well. To make my family wide and far proud, or to see themselves in me, it gives me strength.

This story appears in the Winter issue of Harper’s Bazaar.

#6705. OPI Just Brought Back Dozens of Discontinued Nail Polish Colors. Did Your Favorite Make the Cut?

Walk, don’t run, your next nail appointment... OPI has cracked open its polish vault, and some of the best, previously retired OPI nail polish colors have officially made their comeback. In honor of its 45th anniversary, the brand has brought back about a dozen iconic shades that mani lovers have been begging to see again, plus even more shades inspired by OGs for a grand total of 24 new(ish) polishes.

Meet OPI’s Most Requested Collection, which combines several previously-retired fan favorites with some fresh shades inspired by some of the brand’s most beloved colors. The collection includes everything from vampy Lincoln Park at Midnight and nostalgic pink Mod About You Pastel to Route Beer Float, a very ‘90s, shimmery mauve. This fall 2026 collection includes 24 permanent shades, meaning these colors aren’t just making a brief cameo before disappearing again—they’re back for good. Twelve of them are offered in the classic OPI Nail Lacquer formula, while the other 12 have come back in the longer-lasting Infinite Shine option.

Whether you’re excited to reunite with an old favorite, discover a cult classic you missed the first time around, or try a new shade inspired by some of these icons, I highly recommend giving the full collection a scroll. To get you started, here are 12 shades from this buzzy launch that I’m especially excited to try.

She’s baaaaccckkkkk! The inky purple shade originally launched exactly 20 years ago and is the shimmery sister to one of my all-time faves, Lincoln Park After Dark. You know those polishes that look black until the light hits them? That’s exactly what you’re getting with this ultra moody, ultra iconic shade.

Another shade straight from the vault, this 2012 rich, deep violet with red shimmer became an instant favorite when it originally debuted. If you love burgundy nails for the colder months, consider your next manicure handled.

It may be fall, but not every manicure needs to be dark and moody rn. Mod About You Pastel polish brings a soft, creamy pink into the mix, making it a pretty option for anyone who prefers a sweet, minimalist manicure over the season’s deeper shades. It’s a slightly warmer-toned sister to another one of my faves, Mod About You.

Originally released in 1997, Route Beer Float is the oldest shade OPI brought back for this collection. A mauve-meets-caramel shimmery shade makes it a particularly chic option for the chocolate brown and chai latte manicures that have been everywhere this season.

Quiet luxury nail lovers, this one’s for you. Berlin There, Doin’ That is a creamy, light taupe that puts a fresh spin on OPI’s beloved Berlin There, Done That shade. It’s a little lighter and softer than the original, with a greige-like finish that makes it the perfect understated neutral.

OPI Ink fans, rejoice! Your favorite deep violet is getting a second life with Don’t Over Ink It. The shimmery, deep, inky navy-purple has all the moody, mysterious appeal of the original, but this new version is shimmery rather than sparkly and leans a little more navy. Overall, though, the two are pretty dang similar. Is this your sign to revisit your purple polish era? I think yes.

Say bonjour to your next favorite neutral. This chic, creamy mauve-ish nude pays homage to the beloved Tickle My France-y shade. It’s more of a neutral than its predecessor, which was a much rosier, dusty-rose-meets-mauve shade. It’s soft, sophisticated, and gives your nails that effortlessly polished, je ne sais quoi look. Oui oui!

Did ya miss her? Talk about a throwback... It’s All Greek to Me is back from the archives, bringing its vivid, shimmery fuchsia pink finish along for the ride. The bold, metallic shade makes a statement, so I can see why OPI fans begged for its return. I’m ready to paint a couple coats on my fingertips ahead of the holiday party season. Who says bright pink nails are just for summer?

I do! I do say yes to Suzi Takes a Vow. It’s a soft, romantic peachy pink that’s giving major bridal mani energy. Wedding bells or not, consider this your sign to commit to this classic light neutral.

You know when you just have to try something based on the name alone? That’s how I feel about this one. With a name like Vampire State Building, you already know this is going to be dramatic. The deep burgundy shade—originally released in 2000—delivers all the vampy energy you could want from a dark red manicure.

A lot of the polishes in this new collection are pretty opaque, but this sheer beauty is perfect for a naked nail or soap manicure moment. It’s a soft, pale pink with a barely-there finish that’s tailor-made for the clean girl mani crowd. Think your-nails-but-better, with a little extra wink. See what I did there?

A classic red manicure never goes out of style, and neither does Vodka & Caviar (the nail polish or the food-and-drink combo). The expensive-looking shade is luxury in a bottle. This vibrant apple red looks just as good with jeans and a white tee as it does with your favorite holiday party outfit. Love some versatility!

Catharine Malzahn is a contributing beauty writer at Cosmo. She’s covered and tested all things nails, from the coolest new polish colors to cuticle care and nail art trends.

Catharine Malzahn is a contributing beauty writer at Cosmopolitan and was previously the beauty assistant at Good Housekeeping, Woman's Day, and Prevention.
